newsitem.title: USA: U.S. photographer convicted of sex murder of model.
newsitem.headline: U.S. photographer convicted of sex murder of model.

text.p: A photographer was convicted Friday of raping and murdering a model whose body was found in a shallow grave in a remote wilderness area.

Charles Rathbun, 39, was found guilty of sexually assaulting 27-year-old Linda Sobek with a "foreign object," a so-called special circumstance under California law that means he faces life imprisonment without the possibility of parole.
Sobek left her Hermosa Beach apartment Nov. 16, 1995, for a free-lance modelling assignment and never returned.
The prosecution contended Rathbun raped and then smothered Sobek to prevent her from telling of the crime. He buried her in the Angeles National Forest 50 miles (80 km) northeast of Los Angeles.

Rathbun, a photographer who specialised in picture layouts of fast cars and beautiful women, testified during his trial that Sobek got drunk with him and was killed accidentally during a photo shoot after they had consensual sex. But prosecutors called it a coldblooded murder.
Police found her body in a shallow grave after Rathbun led them to the spot. Sentencing was set for Dec. 16, and defence attorney Mark Werksman said he might consider an appeal.
Outside the courthouse in the Los Angeles suburb of Torrance, he was happy with the verdict the jury reached after six hours of deliberations.
"I hope Rathbun gets his due and suffers...in this life and the next," Sobek's father Bob said outside the court.
Prosecutors decided before the five-week trial not to seek the death penalty because the photographer had no previous convictions and led investigators to the body.
